title: Local Time by Coordinates: Time at a Point
description: Find the local time and time zone for exact coordinates with Local Time by Coordinates — the point's own zone and offset. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a research station, a border farm and a mid-ocean buoy at the same longitude can keep three different clocks — because zones follow politics and land, not just the sun.
quick_answer: Local Time by Coordinates resolves the time zone for an exact pair of coordinates and reports the local time and UTC offset there. Enter the point and read its clock — zone name, offset and DST state — the answer for places with coordinates but no famous city name.

faq: What does this tool calculate?
The time zone, current UTC offset and local time for an exact coordinate pair — resolved from the point itself via the tz database's geography.
Do I need an account?
No — coordinates in, clock out.
Can I use the result for professional work?
For fieldwork, logging and planning, yes — it reads the same tz database systems build on. Contractual deadlines deserve a second confirmation in your own stack.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — you type the coordinates; your device's position is never the input.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Zone borders are political and revise; databases update on their own cycles, so fresh changes can show differently across sources briefly.
What about ocean points?
The tz geography assigns zones at sea too (often Etc/GMT bands or the nearest coast's zone). The answer exists; ships themselves keep their own convention.
Half-hour and 45-minute zones?
Reported exactly — offsets like +5:45 (Nepal) are data, not errors.
Historical times?
Zone rules carry history in the database; a past date at the point can resolve to a different offset. State the date when you ask a different tool to convert.
Solar noon instead?
A different quantity — astronomical, not civil. Sun calculators on this site handle that family; this page is the civil clock.
Can it give a future date's time?
The zone rules project forward — legislatures permitting. The current-rules answer is what the page shows; announced future changes enter the database as they are enacted.
Two points, one zone?
Common — zones are areas, not points. Both points share the rulebook; their solar times still differ by longitude within it.
